Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a chat application written in Rust (a port of the Rails app, compatible with its database). Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

## Layout

| Path | Package | What |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/` | — | `dev`: local server and seed |
| `crates/ruby` | `ruby_compat` | Ruby's own string behaviour the other crates share (ERB escaping, `String#to_i`/`#to_f`/`#strip`, `Float#to_s`, `CGI.escape`, `ERB::Util.url_encode`, Active Record's integer binding, Rack's byte ranges), checked by `vectors/ruby_core.json`; no dependencies |
| `crates/rails_compat` | `rails_compat` | Rails signing/encryption/serialization contracts and the Rails formats several crates write (`ActiveSupport::JSON`, `Content-Disposition`), checked by `vectors/`, and the app's `Clock` (`Time.current`, and time travel for tests) |
| `crates/kit` | `campfire_kit` | Axum adapter, `Ctx`, params, cookies, session, forgery protection, flash, formats, responses, gzip, and the front server (TLS, ACME, HTTP/2, response cache) |
| `crates/routes` | `campfire_routes` | Path helpers for the app's routes |
| `crates/db` | `campfire_db` | rusqlite over the schema, models, queries, fixtures (`fixtures/`) and their loader |
| `crates/richtext` | `campfire_richtext` | Rich text content pipeline: sanitize, attachments, autolink, plain text |
| `crates/storage` | `campfire_storage` | Active Storage-compatible blobs, disk service, variants (libvips), previews (ffmpeg) |
| `crates/cable` | `campfire_cable` | Action Cable protocol server, its WebSocket implementation, and in-process pub/sub |
| `crates/assets` | `campfire_assets` | The frontend (`app/`, `vendor/`, `public/`, `importmap.rb`), digested and embedded at build time |
| `crates/views` | `campfire_views` | Askama templates and view helpers |
| `crates/campfire` | `campfire` (bin) | Controllers, router wiring, channels, jobs, integrations, seeds |

## Working rules

- Rust comes from mise if it isn't on the PATH: `mise exec rust@1.98.1 -- cargo ...` (the version
  in `Dockerfile`).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude html5ever` runs everything. The app's integration tests build
  their seed databases themselves.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude html5ever --all-targets` should stay clean. (`html5ever` is a
  vendored copy with one backported fix and two small additions for Gumbo's parse limits, all
  recorded in its `Cargo.toml`, and identical to upstream otherwise.)
- Format with `cargo fmt --all` (`rustfmt.toml`) before committing, and `bench/loadgen`, a workspace

manage everyone's.

## Data

- A bot is a `users` row with `role = 2` (`Role::Bot`), so it joins rooms, has memberships and
  authors messages like a person. `User::create` grants it every open room after commit.
- Its `bots` row (`campfire_db::Bot`, created by `schema::ADDITIONS`) holds `user_id` (unique),
  `creator_id` and `token`. It's a separate table rather than columns on `users`:
  `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent on every boot, `users` keeps the Rails columns that
  `columns_test` checks, and the Rails image ignores it.
- The bot code is `"<user id>-<token>"` (Rails Campfire's `bot_key` format). The token has 24
  alphanumeric characters. `Bot::authenticate` looks the bot up by id and compares tokens with
  `rails_compat::secure_compare`.
- `password_digest` is `NOT NULL`, so a bot gets the bcrypt digest of a random password. It has no
  email address, so it can't sign in, and session transfers refuse bots.
- Deleting a bot deletes its `bots` row (and its webhook) and deactivates its user, so its messages
  keep their author. Resetting a code (`PATCH /bots/:bot_id/key`) replaces the token.
- A bot's optional webhook is a `bot_webhooks` row (`campfire_db::Webhook`: `bot_id` unique, `url`),
  another `schema::ADDITIONS` table: a column added to `bots` wouldn't reach databases that already
  have the table. `Webhook::assign` strips the URL, deletes the row for a blank one, and otherwise
  validates an absolute `http(s)://` URL with a host (error on `webhook_url`) and upserts.

## Routes

`controllers::app_routes` holds routes Rails doesn't have. They're matched after the whole Rails
table, which stays identical to `vectors/campfire_routes.json`. The route tests seed their corpus
from both tables.

| Route | Action |
|---|---|
| `GET /bots`, `GET /bots/new`, `POST /bots` | list (no pagination, `Cache-Control: no-store`), form, create |
| `GET /bots/:id/edit`, `PATCH/PUT /bots/:id`, `DELETE /bots/:id` | edit, rename/webhook/avatar, delete |
| `PATCH/PUT /bots/:bot_id/key` | new code |
| `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` | the bot API (`messages::by_bots`) |

Bots someone can't manage answer 404 (`Bot::find_manageable_by`).

## The bot API

- The chain skips session authentication and forgery protection. `concerns::authenticate_bot`
  returns 401, then `set_room` returns 404 (an unknown room, or one the bot isn't in). A blank body
  without a multipart `attachment` gets 422. Success is `201` with `Location: /messages/:id`, a path.
- The raw body is the rich-text body, as Rails Campfire's `request.body.read` is. HTML is sanitized
  on render. Creating, broadcasting and push use the composer's `create_message` and
  `broadcast_create`.
- `curl -d` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. kit would reject bodies like `100% done` as
  malformed params before routing. `by_bots::read_raw_body`, a middleware in `app::router`, parses
  the body for this path and drops param errors.
- `by_bots::filter_key` is the `PathFilter` that `KitConfig::filter_logged_path` and
  `FrontConfig::filter_logged_path` use, so request logs show the code as `[FILTERED]`.

  `account_edit_*.html` and `facts.json` (`bot.svg`) were updated for it.

  accessible name contains "bot code".

steps.message:
Bots no longer join open rooms by default, the bot form (new and edit) has an "Add to all open rooms" switch, and a bot's webhook gets one `joined` event for each room it's added to. All tests pass except `campfire_storage`'s `pipeline_matches_the_vectors`, which fails the same way without my changes (it looks like the image-processing library in this environment). I couldn't run `cargo fmt` or `cargo clippy` because the components aren't installed and there's no network, so I kept lines under the 140-character limit by hand. Run both before committing.

**How it behaves**
- **New bots** start in no rooms. People still join every open room as before.
- **Switch on:** the bot joins every open room that exists, and later every new open room and every closed room that's made open.
- **Switch off:** the bot keeps the rooms it's already in. If the switch isn't in the request at all, the setting stays as it is.
- **Storage:** the setting is a new table, `bots_in_all_open_rooms`, created on boot like the existing bot tables. The Rails app ignores it.
- **`joined`:** it fires only when a membership is actually created. That covers automatic joins and people adding the bot to a closed room. Saving a room again or turning the switch on a second time sends nothing extra. Direct rooms never send it. A bot that's removed from a room and added back gets `joined` again; that's my reading of "whenever a bot is added".
- **Replies:** a `200` text or HTML reply to `joined` is posted into that room as the bot's message, the same way mention replies are.

**One difference from mention replies:** `joined` is sent from a background job with no web request to copy settings from, so the reply's live update is built with Rails' default address, `http://example.org`. Message display doesn't use full URLs, so nothing visible changes, but it isn't taken from the request the way mention replies are.

**UI changes**
- The switch is a real checkbox inside a `<label>` with the visible text "Add to all open rooms". The app's usual switch shrinks its checkbox to zero size, which browser tests can treat as hidden. I added a CSS modifier, `switch__input--cover`, that lays the checkbox transparently over this switch so it has a size and receives clicks. Other switches are unchanged.
- I changed the bots page text that said "Bots join every open room", and the webhook hint now mentions being added to a room.

**Tests:** I added model tests in `crates/db/src/tests/bot_test.rs` and request tests in the bots test file covering the cases above. The existing mention tests assumed bots were in HQ automatically. They now put the bot in HQ with a direct database insert, so a `joined` call doesn't hit their fake server. `README.md` and `docs/bots.md` are updated with the design notes.
